facts.text: The American cranberry, Vaccinium macrocarpon, is native to the wetlands of central and eastern North America; Native Americans gathered it from peat bogs and marshes before colonists came. Growers flood the bogs at harvest and the berries, each holding pockets of air, float. Fresh cranberries are harvested from mid-September through mid-November, in time for Thanksgiving, though the record does not show them at the first feast; the USDA National Agricultural Library notes no clear precedent.
